Summarize a panglm fit

Source: R/summary.R
summary.panglm.Rd

Produces a classic coefficient table (Estimate, Std. Error, z value, Pr(>|z|)) in the style of summary.glm().

Usage

# S3 method for class 'panglm'
summary(object, ...)

Arguments

object

a "panglm" object

...

unused

Value

an object of class "summary.panglm", a list with components call (the matched call), model, effect, and family (as stored on the fit), coefficients (a numeric matrix with one row per parameter and columns Estimate, Std. Error, z value, Pr(>|z|)), nobs, n_groups, df.residual, loglik, dispersion (NULL when not applicable, as for negative binomial fits), iterations, and vcov_type (which covariance estimator produced the reported standard errors). It has an associated print.summary.panglm() method and is normally printed rather than used programmatically. Also included are sigma (random-intercept standard deviation) and shape (gamma shape) when estimated, varcomp (covariance matrix of the random intercept and slopes) for random-slope fits, for family = "negbin" the NB2 negbin_theta (variance mu + mu^2 / theta) of pooled, fixed-effects and random-slope fits, with its standard error negbin_theta_se (pooled and fixed-effects fits, from the observed information at the fitted means, as in MASS::glm.nb()), or negbin_ab, the beta mixing parameters a and b of the random-intercept model, and, for cre = TRUE fits, cre_test: the Wald (Mundlak) test that the individual-mean coefficients are jointly zero, computed with the covariance stored on the fit.

See also

Other panglm methods: confint.panglm(), effectcurve(), fitted.panglm(), glance.panglm(), logLik.panglm(), model.matrix.panglm(), partialeffects.panordered(), plot.panglm(), plot.panglm_effectcurve(), predict.panglm(), predict.panordered(), tidy.panglm(), vcov.panglm()

Examples

data(copd)
fit <- panglm(fev1 ~ treatment + age + smoker + crp, data = copd,
              index = c("id", "visit"), model = "pooling", family = "gaussian")
summary(fit)
#> 
#> Call:
#> panglm(formula = fev1 ~ treatment + age + smoker + crp, data = copd, 
#>     index = c("id", "visit"), model = "pooling", family = "gaussian")

#> age         -0.014239   0.003133  -4.545  5.5e-06 ***
#> smoker      -0.355207   0.055905  -6.354  2.1e-10 ***
#> crp         -0.032895   0.013135  -2.504 0.012269 *
